rules.startup: Process launch and architecture-specific transport availability. This is process lifecycle, not query latency.
rules.machine_index: Machine-global dependency/JDK index lifecycle. JVMD reports machine_cold, daemon_restart and resident_daemon separately; servers without an equivalent report n/a.
rules.initialize: LSP initialize request send to initialize response receive, followed by initialized notification.
rules.service_ready: A server-native normal-service readiness signal such as JDTLS ServiceReady. It is not assumed equivalent to machine indexing or target semantic warmup.
rules.session_open: Workspace session establishment. For JVMD this is distinct from daemon startup and machine-index readiness.
rules.workspace_resolution: Project/model/module/classpath/source-root resolution. Exact boundaries may be unavailable; server-native resolver evidence must be reported instead of substituted.
rules.workspace_index: Workspace-local source/build-artifact indexing or reconciliation. Machine dependency indexing is explicitly excluded. If no authoritative completion barrier exists, readiness is reported unavailable.
rules.document_admission: Open/change notifications through an observable current-document/version boundary. Diagnostics and other work occurring here are attributed rather than silently treated as query latency.
rules.first_use: First request of the measured operation/target after declared preparation. No operation-specific warmup may precede it.
rules.warmup: Symmetric operation-specific requests retained in raw reports but excluded from steady statistics.
rules.steady: Measured operation samples after warmup; only correct samples contribute to comparative latency percentiles.

lifecycle.sessionOpen: not directly observable through the external jvmd-lsp process; see jvmd-machine-lifecycle report for exact native RPC timing
lifecycle.workspaceResolution: not directly timestamped by CMP-01; see jvmd-machine-lifecycle resolver evidence
lifecycle.workspaceIndexReady: unavailable for JVMD: local module refresh is asynchronous and no all-current barrier is exposed

nativeReadiness.equivalence: none claimed; these are server-native milestones at different architectural layers

documentAdmission.boundary: exact-version publishDiagnostics observed for each requested document version
